comments.content: Change all the cautions to warnings please as per what I've been saying for weeks
This looks like the only main difference is this sufficient?
I guess in this situation it shouldn't close the pull. Seems a bit abrasive.
Caution where we need to triage. Warning for all user errors

To be more precise it would make a lot more sense to rename the methods as `clientError` and `serverError` as I proposed many times. 
I didn't think error and fatal would be so subjective but as I understand everybody keeps making it render as caution.

I'm open to the triage logic being elsewhere but the idea is that we'll be able to focus our attention immediately on bug fixes. We can also dynamically prioritize based on the amount of hits a bug gets.

comments.content: Fine with the changes, please address my comments.
Was `organization` targeting the org where the action originated from instead of the actual linked pull-request repo, am I understanding this right?
A detail but might be preferable to just display urls (`closingIssues: closingIssues.map(o => o.url)`) because that can quickly enlarge the logs and lower readability when debugging.
I actually don't understand how this could work before, `owner` is an object and it is passed below in `fetchIssue` which expects a string.

What difference is there with `${organization}/${repository}#${number}` and `${repository.owner.login}/${repository.name}#${number}`, I guess the later also works for individual repo, not only organizations?
Thanks for the fix. I noticed in the bot comment that there is not metadata at all, which doesn't help for debugging? is this plugin not using the SDK to post comments at all?

@0x4007 I think closing the pr makes it clear to contributors that the task is not for them to take, otherwise they would keep working on it. Also, that would make us manually close them before rewards.

Tested with a few different PRs from cross repos, sorry if it is unclear I was testing locally as I don't have any more credits: https://github.com/Meniole/daemon-pull-review/pull/10#issuecomment-2726428182
Seems to use the proper target.
Wouldn't it make sense to use `fatal` for triage and `error` for errors?
Why not adding a capability to the SDK that would do the triage on fatal errors instead? This capability does not belong to a logger package.
